## Introduction

In this notebook, we are reverse engineering the story, [CEOs gave heavily during legislative session, exposing loophole in NC's fundraising ban](https://www.wral.com/archive/17716104/)

## Load libraries

Loading required libraries for this analysis.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Turn off scientific notation
options(scipen=999)

# load your libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(refinr)
library(janitor)
library(stringr)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)

```

## Load and Cleaning Data

In this section, describe the source of the data, write a basic data dictionary for data you are working with, and discuss any caveats or issues you discovered working with this data.

```{r}
# Load required data

nc_finance_data <- read_excel("data/donors0103-0701.xlsx")

# Path to data should be loaded from folder "data" i.e. read_csv("data/name_of_data.csv")

# Clean required data and prepare for analysis if needed. 

nc_finance_data <- nc_finance_data |> 
  rename(name_clean = "name-clean")

```

## Sentences to Engineer

In this notebook, we are reverse engineering five sentences from the story.

### Sentence 1

- **Sentence text**: The co-chief executives at a Georgia firm that brokers tax credits put \$41,000 into the campaign accounts of North Carolina General Assembly members during the last regular legislative session.
- **Analysis summary**: We filtered by names of the two CEOs, GEORGE LEWIS STROBEL II and ROBIN E DELMER for the dates of the short legislative session in 2018, which was from May 16 to June 29. We also filtered for donations made to candidates. We found that, combined, the two men had donated a combined \$41,250, which matches the original finding exactly.

```{r}
# Put code to reverse engineer sentence here
session_nc_finance_data <- nc_finance_data |> 
  filter(between(date, as.Date("2018-05-16"), as.Date("2018-06-29")))

session_nc_finance_data |> 
  filter((name_clean == "GEORGE LEWIS STROBEL II" | name_clean == "ROBIN E DELMER") & source == "candidates") |> 
  group_by(name_clean) |> 
  summarise(
    total = sum(amount)
  )


# Display results of code below this codeblock

```

### Sentence 3

- **Sentence text**: Despite loopholes, it's clear the partial session ban depresses fundraising. Giving peaks right before session, then falls off a cliff. 
- **Analysis summary**: The graph we made highlights how fundraising drops off right before the weeks of the session begins in May. This confirms the findings from the story.

```{r}
# Put code to reverse engineer sentence here
nc_finance_data_by_date <- nc_finance_data |>
  mutate(week = week(date),
         #week = as.Date(paste(2018, week, 1, sep = "-"), "%Y-%U-%u")
         week_num = floor_date(date, "week")
    ) |> 
  group_by(week_num) |> 
  summarise(
    total = sum(amount)
  )


nc_finance_data_by_date |>
  ggplot() + 
  geom_line(aes(x=week_num, y=total)) +
  scale_x_datetime(date_breaks = "2 week", date_labels = "%b %d") + 
  labs(
    x = "Weeks",
    y = "Amount ($)",
    title = "Amount of money donated to NC State Legislature in first half of 2018",
    caption = "Source: NC campaign finance data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()




# Display results of code below this codeblock

```

### Sentence 4

- **Sentence text**: This year's legislative session also saw significant donations from hog farmers and beer distributors, both industries with important legislation before the General Assembly. Senate President Pro Tem Phil Berger's campaign alone raised nearly \$222,000 during session. Twenty-three people gave him the maximum allowed: $5,200.
- **Analysis summary**: By filtering for Berger within the session finance data, we found the \$222,000 donated to his campaign. We then did an additional filter on amount, looking for people who had donated \$5,200 to Berger's campaign, and we found that 23 people had given that amount. Both of these findings confirm the data in the story.

```{r}
# Put code to reverse engineer sentence here

session_nc_finance_data |> 
  filter(committee_name == "PHILIP E BERGER COMM") |> 
  summarise(
    total = sum(amount)
  )


session_nc_finance_data |> 
  filter(amount == 5200 & committee_name == "PHILIP E BERGER COMM") |> 
  group_by(name_clean) |> 
  summarise(
    count = n()
  )


# Display results of code below this codeblock

```
